references.text: The same Pharisees who receive the message in John 11:46 immediately gather for a council meeting to discuss the consequences of Jesus' actions and plot his death.
The report about Jesus' miracles leads the religious leaders to plan not only to kill Jesus, but also Lazarus, who is the concrete proof of the miracle.
As a result of some people going to the Pharisees and reporting what Jesus did, they decided from that day on to put him to death.
In the Gospel of Mark, some also report Jesus' deeds to the religious leaders, triggering a conspiracy to destroy him.
Luke describes a similar situation where the chief priests and scribes seek a way to destroy Jesus because the people are listening to his teaching and witnessing his miracles.
